data.one_liner: Comprehensive pure-Dart cryptography and blockchain toolkit with optional Rust backend.
data.what_it_does: Provides core utilities for hashing, encoding, cryptography curves, mnemonics, HD wallets, addresses, and transaction signers across multiple blockchains. Supports a dual backend allowing execution in pure Dart or Rust (FFI/WASM).
use_when: You are building a cryptocurrency wallet or interacting with blockchain networks.
You need robust cryptographic functions, key derivation, or address encoding in Dart.
You require cross-platform support for blockchain primitives with optional performance backends.
avoid_when: You only need a simple, single-purpose library like standard base58 or bip39 and want to minimize dependency weight.
You need production-verified real hardware wallet communication without simulation testing.
strengths: Comprehensive coverage of blockchain networks, curve types, and encoding formats.
Dual backend architecture supporting pure Dart or high-performance Rust execution.
Extensive support for zero-knowledge, threshold signatures, and Zcash protocols.
weaknesses: Hardware wallet flows are simulation-tested only and not verified with real devices yet.
Breaking changes in major versions require migration (e.g. unified BuError types, API restructuring).
data.setup_notes: Pure Dart by default. Optional Rust backend requires loading platform dynamic libraries or WASM assets.

alternatives.name: web3dart
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you specifically need a dedicated Ethereum-focused client and JSON-RPC provider library.

alternatives.name: bip39
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you only need basic BIP39 mnemonic generation without a massive multi-chain cryptographic toolkit.
